1192600197886627840.a: Cronies? GAO procurement policies? Lowest bidder? You have millions of idiots building IT systems that look like PCs. Some clearly in use by critical infrastructure. This is inappropriate. You need separation of concerns in hardware. Don't rely on some TPM chip and crap software.

1192600936960741376.a: If it takes 5 CPUs, multiple physically isolated memory bank, faraday cages, noise gens, etc in your router to make it secure then sobeit. That does not cost substantially more to make any more. It requires qualified developers. We lack those. We need to teach developers security

1192601805433249792.a: You want to see how separation of concerns works in a virtual environment? Go download QubesOS and install it on the proper hardware. That's how you separate concerns in software. Now de-virtualize it and build real hardware that way as well. Limit each component to its purpose.

1192602515667210241.a: Generalizing all of your security infrastructure hardware and then forcing software to do all the work of security is like trying to breathe with your liver. Maybe you figure out a way using a clever hack but it is likely to be fragile and unpredictable.

1192605560560070661.a: Most routers I have seen for the last 10-15 years run the network stack under Linux on a general purpose CPU. Why? Why do you need an OS at all to route packets? You need a network hardware driver, network stack, and a _read-only_ configuration dataset. The end. Single threaded.

1192605562460155904.a: So, you want to configure the router... Cool. You have another onboard system which can manipulate the config dataset out of band. Those two must never physically be able to communicate. Again, this one needs a single threaded offline terminal accepting config commands. The end.

1192605564335001600.a: But hey we want a web interface that allows the router to be configured. Really? Do you? Fine, let's say that makes sense. That web interface connects to the config computer's serial terminal using a crypted hardware bus and issues audited commands. Single threaded software.

1192605565740093440.a: Lets say this router needs a network switch. Hey let's just slap that onto the router's kernel network stack, right? No. Again, single threaded dedicated network switch on its own CPU, own RAM, etc. The router's only connection to it is via Ethernet or a dedicated crypted bus.

1192605567291920385.a: Build your IT systems like an organism so they are resilient against attack. Assume everything is always compromised. Trust nothing. Least of all your hardware, yourself, and your developers. Audit everything all the time and have watchdogs monitors the audit log always.

1192606757710913541.a: One last thing, you remembered to write the firmware for each of these separate components in a type-safe language, right? oCaml or something that will protect you from memory leaks, overruns, etc... This compulsion to treat everything as if it were a 90s PC rots our technology.
